name: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
title: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
answer: Local and air-gapped model deployment means running an AI model on hardware that the organization controls, rather than calling a vendor's API over the public internet. Local deployment can still have network access, while air-gapped deployment keeps the system physically disconnected from external networks. In legal operations this pattern is used for tasks such as contract review, document summarization, privilege review, and e-discovery, where client confidences and legal privilege are at stake. It also appears in regulated settings where data cannot leave a controlled environment. The scope covers the model weights, the runtime, the hardware, and the surrounding workflow for document handling.

sections.body: Local and air-gapped model deployment means running an AI model on hardware that the organization controls, rather than calling a vendor's API over the public internet. Local deployment can still have network access, while air-gapped deployment keeps the system physically disconnected from external networks. In legal operations this pattern is used for tasks such as contract review, document summarization, privilege review, and e-discovery, where client confidences and legal privilege are at stake. It also appears in regulated settings where data cannot leave a controlled environment. The scope covers the model weights, the runtime, the hardware, and the surrounding workflow for document handling.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The infrastructure typically includes one or more servers or workstations with sufficient memory and compute, often GPUs for larger models. Common runtimes include llama.cpp, Ollama, and vLLM, which can load open-weight models such as those from the Llama or Mistral families. Air-gapped setups require offline copies of model weights, container images, and software packages, because the machine cannot reach public repositories. Updates and patches must be moved in by approved media or through a controlled staging area. Storage, backup, and logging systems also sit inside the same boundary.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work begins with selecting a model that fits the task and the available hardware, then obtaining the weights and any necessary licenses. The team installs the runtime, configures it for the local environment, and tests the model against a set of representative legal documents. For retrieval-augmented generation, a local vector database and embedding model are added so the system can cite internal sources. Prompts and evaluation criteria are developed and versioned, and outputs are logged for review. Integration with document management or case management systems is done through local APIs or file exchanges.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on data residency, confidentiality, and the provenance of the model itself. Open-weight models come with licenses that may restrict commercial use or require attribution, and the training data behind them can carry its own legal exposure. Air-gapped systems reduce some network risks but introduce patching and monitoring challenges, because the organization must track vulnerabilities without automatic updates. Audit trails, access controls, and ethical walls must be maintained inside the environment. The site's 215 compliance and regulation pages reflect the many overlapping rules, from data protection laws to state AI bills, that can bear on where and how legal data is processed.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction of travel is toward smaller, more efficient models that can run on modest hardware without a network connection. Quantization and distillation techniques are making local deployment more practical for legal teams that cannot send data to a cloud service. Confidential computing and trusted execution environments may allow sensitive inference even in shared or remote infrastructure. We are likely to see more turnkey air-gapped appliances and reference architectures aimed at legal operations. Regulation and client expectations will continue to shape how these systems are documented and audited.
